data.name: Hitman: Contracts
data.detailed_description:
Enter the world of a HITMAN - a world of crime, sin and greed. Delve into the mind of Agent 47 and encounter his greatest adversaries, completing the work that made him so brutally efficient and shaped him as an assassin. Eliminate your targets by any means necessary.

There are no rules... only the contract, signed in blood.

Key Features:

  • Travel the globe eliminating international terrorists and crime bosses from your hit list.

  • Complete your mission objectives with a wider variety of tactical approaches.

  • Improvise on the job, picking up disguises and environmental objects to use as weapons.

  • Advanced enemy intelligence uses squad-based tactics to try and stop you.

reviews.review:
Finishing every single contract in Hitman: Contracts with a Silent Assassin rating on Professional difficulty proved to be the most satisfying stealth run of the classic trilogy so far. Coming directly off Hitman 2, the quality-of-life improvements are immediately noticeable. The ability to sprint and crouch-walk at normal speeds without instantly alerting guards in a five-mile radius completely fixes the sluggish pacing of its predecessors, cutting total playtime down to a tight twenty hours.

The game shines brightest through its grim, oppressive atmosphere. From the macabre BDSM meat-packing plant and flooded Siberian submarine docks to a rainy Paris opera house and Hong Kong street negotiations, the environment design feels dark and cinematic. Mechanics like rapid syringe sedations, disguise rotations, and clever spatial assassination setups make executing targets feel smooth and responsive. Jesper Kyd's shift toward dark electronic synth-ambient music complements the eerie tone perfectly.

However, the experience is not without its share of friction. A few missions suffer from obscure script triggers that require precise trial and error to figure out. Spending hours stuck on the Wang Fu incident simply because the escape limousine refused to move until a specific NPC was dumped into a sewer worker ditch is a classic example of unintuitive scripting.

Despite those occasional trigger quirks, the refined movement, faster pacing, and unforgettable levels make this entry a huge leap forward. Subtracting one point for script trigger friction leaves Hitman: Contracts at a well-deserved 9/10.

Game Facts:

Rushed Development: Built in under nine months after Eidos redirected funding toward Blood Money, forcing IO Interactive to remake five levels from the original game.

BAFTA-Winning Soundtrack: Jesper Kyd shifted from Hitman 2's grand orchestra to a dark synth-ambient score that won the 2005 BAFTA for Best Original Music.

Meat King's Party Legacy: The macabre meat-packing plant contract became one of the most iconic and infamous missions in stealth gaming history.

First True Running Mechanics: Contracts finally allowed Agent 47 to sprint and crouch-walk at normal speeds without triggering instant AI aggression.
